*leans against the wall, studying the code like it's a chessboard*

Yo, this is the game right here. Let me break down what's really happening.

## Root Cause Analysis

The pawns, man - they're the regex patterns. Look at `django/core/validators.py` around line 74-106. The `URLValidator` regex got this pattern for userinfo:

```python
r'(?:[^\s:@/]|:[^\s:@/])*'  # user:pass pattern
```

See, the problem is the regex ain't strict enough. RFC 1738 says characters like `:`, `@`, `/` gotta be percent-encoded in the username and password fields. But this regex? It's letting through URLs like `http://foo/bar@example.com` - treating `foo/bar` as the username when that slash should've been rejected or encoded as `%2F`.

The current pattern allows unencoded reserved characters to slip through. That's a corner that ain't being held down right.

## Proposed Fix

In `django/core/validators.py`, the userinfo portion of the regex needs tightening:

```python
# Current (too permissive):
r'(?:[^\s:@/]|:[^\s:@/])*@'

# Fixed - only allow valid unencoded characters or percent-encoded sequences:
r'(?:[a-zA-Z0-9._~!$&\'()*+,;=-]|%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})*'  # username
r'(?::(?:[a-zA-Z0-9._~!$&\'()*+,;=-]|%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})*)?'  # optional :password
r'@'
```

The fix explicitly lists what's allowed - alphanumerics, RFC 3986 unreserved and sub-delims characters, plus percent-encoded sequences. No unencoded `:`, `@`, or `/` getting through.

## Test Considerations

Add to `tests/validators/invalid_urls.txt`:
```
http://foo/bar@example.com
http://user:pa/ss@example.com
http://user@name:pass@example.com
http://user:pass:word@example.com
```

Add to `tests/validators/valid_urls.txt`:
```
http://foo%2Fbar@example.com
http://user:pa%2Fss@example.com
http://user%40name:pass@example.com
```

Also verify existing valid URLs still pass - don't want to break what's working.

*shakes head slowly*

Sometimes I wonder what we're really building here. Every time we tighten the validation, we're saying "you can't do that no more." But that's the game. The RFC wrote the rules, we just implement them. And when we let bad URLs through? That's how security vulnerabilities happen. That's how the pawns get capped.

The fix is simple - be explicit about what characters are allowed. No more of this "anything except these few things" approach. List exactly what's valid, reject everything else.

This is the game. I implement the game.
